newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy train derailment kills at least eight.
newsitem.headline: Italy train derailment kills at least eight.

text.p: At least eight people died on Sunday when a high-speed train hurtled off the track and crashed into electricity pylons in northern Italy.
Police and firemen at the scene said more victims could still be inside the tangled wreckage of the Milan to Rome express.
State railways said in a statement eight people had been confirmed dead at 1515 GMT -- nearly three hours after the accident -- and 25 were injured.
The "Pendolino," Italy's fastest train, derailed as it was approaching the station of Piacenza, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Milan.
The statement said seven of the train's eight carriages had derailed.
Witnesses said the first was completely ripped open and the sixth still upright but crushed between the fifth and seventh carriages. The train hit a number of pylons before it came to a halt.
The cause of the accident was not immediately known but media reports said the tilting train had been approaching the station too fast after a curve.
It had not been due to stop at Piacenza.

"The train was going very fast and all of a sudden we found ourselves lying sideways. It was terrible," a member of the crew told Italian radio. "Fortunately, I was at the end of the train," he added.
The train had crossed a bridge over the River Po minutes before.
The victims had not been definitively identified but they were all believed to be Italian.
A railway official at the scene said the dead were belived to be two conductors, an on-board hostess, three railway police and two other passengers.
Former president Francesco Cossiga was aboard the train but escaped unhurt. "I heard a big bang and all of a sudden I was on the floor," he told reporters.
The train had left Milan at 1230 GMT and was due to arrive in Rome at 1620 GMT.
The accident blocked rail traffic in both directions on the main north-south link.
The railways statement said trains to and from northern Italy were being re-routed via other cities.
The accident came less than two weeks after four people were killed in a train accident near the northern city of Brescia.
